title: Air-Gapped Workflow Automation: A Guide for Secure Networks
summary: Air gapped workflow automation requires specific infrastructure configurations to maintain strict data isolation while managing internal task processing.
body_markdown:
## Deploying self-hosted automation with Activepieces


Activepieces provides a sovereign automation engine that executes workflows entirely within a private infrastructure, eliminating the requirement for external telemetry or third-party cloud triggers.


A stripped self-hosted build is how most vendors monetise control, but Activepieces does not sell a smaller product to the buyers who need the most control; SSO, SCIM, custom RBAC, audit logs, release management and secret manager integration run in the air-gapped build exactly as they do in the managed cloud.


### Deploying the engine using docker compose


To instantiate the core engine, a standard Docker Compose configuration is all that is required to run[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces) on-premise, alongside a Postgres database for persistence and a Redis instance for task queuing.


Because the core is MIT-licensed, you can inspect the source code to verify that no "phone-home" beacons exist.


Internal mission-critical triggers, such as a local GitLab webhook, never leave the perimeter. This architectural autonomy means you aren't beholden to a SaaS provider’s maintenance window.


As the local administrator, the security of the underlying host remains your primary responsibility. This is a significant undertaking given the 650 Critical CVEs documented by the Linux CVE Tracker. 6,519 High CVEs and 9,489[Medium](https://medium.com/@thunikiakilesh/how-i-automated-multi-tenant-saas-infrastructure-on-aws-using-terraform-no-manual-setup-87d6c4af49d7) CVEs are also reported by the tracker.


For the local administrator, a rigorous, automated patching cycle is the only way to maintain the integrity of the air-gap.


### Managing secrets and local integrations without the cloud


Every credential Activepieces touches (API keys, OAuth tokens, and connection secrets) can be routed to your own secret manager instead of a vendor database. This ensures that in the self-hosted edition, no third party ever holds the credentials your business runs on.


This allows the engine to interface with local LLMs, such as Mistral Large 4 or GPT-6 Astra via a private proxy, without exposing API keys to the open internet.


You will find 739 integrations available for local installation within the Activepieces "Integrations" library view, roughly 60% of which are community-contributed, meaning the majority of your automation support relies on volunteer maintenance rather than official vendor backing.


This modularity ensures that you can drag a connector for a local SQL Server or a private instance of Mattermost into a flow without the connector ever reaching out to a public package registry.


### Enterprise governance: SSO and audit logs for regulated teams


While the Community edition supports unlimited local runs, regulated teams typically require the Enterprise tier to satisfy specific compliance controls like AC-2 and AU-2.


Activepieces provides the same governance features (SSO, SCIM, custom RBAC, audit logs, and release management) in the air-gapped build as it does in the managed cloud. Detailed audit logs capture every execution and configuration change, providing the "who, what, and when" necessary for forensic review.


Regulated organizations like MoneyGram and FundingSocieties run this architecture in production today to ensure air-gapped environments maintain full control rather than a fraction of the platform's capability.
